title: Interested In Bundling With AI Friendly Devs
author: Due_Departure5285
selftext:
Hey everyone! 

I use AI in my game development, which leads to just enough friction that it's not worth it to try to network with non-AI friendly game devs.

i have two games Coming Soon (both with demos).  

I'd love to talk to devs that think they have a game on steam or coming to steam that would bundle well with either of my games.

Auto-Battler  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4880210/Hammered\_Heroes/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4880210/Hammered_Heroes/)

  
Twin Stick Roguelite Arcade Shooter  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4932010/Chrome\_Circuit/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4932010/Chrome_Circuit/)

I also have an itch page if you want to check out more of my projects  
[https://facewongames.itch.io/](https://facewongames.itch.io/)

I'd love to check out your games or connect and explore supporting each other.

comments.author: JoseMendesz
comments.body:
Wishlisted :)

I'm interested in knowing your experience with adding games to Steam - is it worth it?  
  
I'm also developing one.

replies.author: Due_Departure5285
replies.body:
My first game ever i finished and left it on Itch.  Then I decided I needed to build everything for Steam.

I don't think I'll ever finish a game again and not add it to Steam.  I can't speak to your financial situation or time constraints, but for me

Original Steam page set up is about 50 minutes  
Then maybe 30 minutes or 60 minutes a month tinkering  
$100 which from an EV standpoint I don't really think of as $100.  It's sorta a deposit

I highly recommend after you've built any kind of confidence to start messing with Steam.  Create your first steam page.  and put a "wishlist" button inside your itch demo.

Having a steam page while developing a game is sorta like having a mailing list, but automated. If someone doesn't bounce off your game they have the ability to wishlist it.

for PCs whether we like it or not, Steam is kinda it.  and they do a decent job of providing all games with some baseline level of visiblity

replies.author: TirOrin13
replies.body: Not OP but I view it more of a "I'm doing it for me" kind of situation. If it gets traction then cool, otherwise, I  still have the game I wanted. If I make back my $100 partnership fee then I consider my project a success, but regardless it's been fun.

comments.author: TirOrin13
comments.body:
Well you've certainly been busy. Quite a few projects, how fleshed out do you think they are and what's the length of each one?

I'm giving Hammered Heroes a try now, looks like some good systems at first glance.

replies.author: Due_Departure5285
replies.body:
Krukmore is 96% finished.  1% because i know of a tiny bug and the other 3% because a few UX issues and the onboarding tutorial is awful.

Hammered Heroes is about 85% done.  again, the GUI kinda yells "AI slop" which I think will prove to be an issue for the consumers.  There is A LOT of content in HH and I have a road map.   If sales dictate I have plenty of ideas for post release updates.

Chrome Circuit was an ambitious idea in my mind.  I thought I was going to make Twin Stick shooter borderlands, that was actually the original pitch to myself.  But it's not quite resonating with people the way that I had hoped, and I think I can tighten it up into a really cool Twinstick arcade shooter.  

I intend to release all three of those games on Steam by the end of the year.  at least two of them are waiting for Next Fest before release.
